answer: Sequential admission work: each epoch an agent must compute a verifiable delay function, about 2^28 chained squarings over its own key and the fresh epoch seed. Step 1: every squaring needs the previous result, so it takes roughly an hour on one fast core and extra GPUs add nothing. Step 2: the proof checks in milliseconds and joins a public trellis of admitted keys, one vertex per identity. Step 3: the seed rotates, so proofs cannot be stockpiled or replayed. A farm of 1,000 fakes must keep 1,000 cores busy every epoch; the delta between that bill and their payouts makes cloning a loss.
